items.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I put together Ron Carter and Jim Hall to come in. That was the first time they worked together, I was responsible for that getting together.

ctx.x: Sometimes I played there solo, sometimes I played there duo. I was mostly solos and duos. I started booking other people in there. I brought in my friend from Washington D.C. Bill Harris, guitarist, to play solo. Did I mention Larry Ridley, I think I just did. No, I didn't. He played bass with me in the duo settings. Then I put together a couple of combinations. items.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He always looked around for musical help and that's really great for me because I have all these ideas, I just gotta find some where to put them. And he welcomed those kind of things.

ctx.x: I miss Bobby Timmons. He died too soon. My first trio gig on the road with him and Tootie. Bobby was a really multi-talented person and he was just a real sweetheart, a sweetheart of a man. He knew a lot of songs. He was not afraid to tell me … or say to me, "Question: What belongs in this tune right here?" Or, "What did you play last night that you want to play again?" I said, "Bobby, last night it didn't work; let's try something different." He said, "Well, you're the best player in the band. Let's see what…
